title: MCP2551 CAN and Logics
summary: Wire a classic CAN transceiver and use asynchronous transmit, receive and status nodes.
body: Windows 0.1.84 testing adds MCP2551 under Communication for full-feature ESP32, ESP32-S2, ESP32-S3 and ESP32-C3 firmware. One controller/transceiver is supported. Add the peripheral, assign CTX/CRX and compile the selected board. Compact firmware and ESP8266 do not expose these nodes.

Electrical connection

MCP2551 requires 5 V power. Connect GND to common ground, CTX to the transmit GPIO, and CRX to the receive GPIO through a 5 V to 3.3 V level shifter. CANH/CANL connect only to the external bus. Verify onboard level shifting and termination: the Fritzing artwork is not a circuit guarantee. Use 120-ohm termination at each end of the bus.

Logics nodes

Configure selects 125/250/500/1000 kbit/s and listen-only mode. Startup defaults to 500 kbit/s listen-only. Disable Listen only to transmit and acknowledge. Send queues one single-attempt classic CAN frame with a decimal identifier and up to eight space-separated hex bytes. Extended identifiers and remote requests are supported. Remote frames use Length and empty Data. Queued does not mean delivered.

Received exposes the latest identifier, flags, length and hex data. Identifier filter -1 accepts all frames. Fast bursts can coalesce between Logics ticks. Status reports Ready, Bus off and RX-missed/TX-failed counters. Correct wiring and bitrate before using Configure to restart after bus-off. Reconfiguration clears queues and resets counters.

Example: On Start → Configure (Listen only false) → Send. Received.Out → MQTT Publish.In; Received.Data → Publish.Text. This supports classic CAN, not CAN-FD or higher-level protocol decoding. Physical testing requires the transceiver and another CAN node.
